newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco mayor will slash deficit-spokesman.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco mayor will slash deficit-spokesman.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown's office said on Thursday spending would be adjusted to eliminate the city's projected budget shortfall of $107 million for next year.
"What the mayor's budget staff is doing right now is making policy decisions. The budget is a work in progress," said P.J. Johnston, the mayor's spokesman.
"Mayor Brown will deliver on time a balanced budget," he added.
City budget officials on Wednesday announced that San Francisco faces a budget deficit next year of $107 million.
The initial budget forecast showed the city with $67 million in red ink when the current rate of spending was compared with expected revenues in fiscal year 1997-1998.
In addition, welfare cutbacks in Washington and Sacramento are expected to cost the city an additional $40 million.
Brown must submit a budget to the board of supervisors on June 1 for the 1997-1998 fiscal year.
